original_question: For every previously introduced model whose existence theory is still open, determine whether necessary or sufficient conditions guarantee uniqueness of the solution once existence is obtained.
target_in_paper: Open Problem 38 (§4.1.2, Considerations): "The following question can be proposed for any previously introduced model with existence as an open problem: Do there exist necessary and/or sufficient conditions that guarantee the uniqueness of the solution obtained?"
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s official formulation. It correctly captures the universal scope over earlier models in the paper whose existence theory is still open, the focus on uniqueness only after an existence result is available, and the paper’s emphasis on identifying necessary and/or sufficient conditions rather than merely asking whether uniqueness holds.
missing_details: The paper states this as a reusable model-by-model open problem for any previously introduced model with existence still open, not as one single simultaneous classification theorem covering all such models at once.
In the surrounding context, uniqueness means uniqueness of the non-trivial solution.
For time-dependent problems, uniqueness is explicitly understood as uniqueness for a given initial condition.
The relevant solution concept is not fixed globally; depending on the model, one may need classical, weak, strong, or mild solutions.
A stand-alone formulation should say that the domain, boundary conditions, and initial data are those attached to the particular earlier model being studied.

The specific operators and hypotheses are inherited from the chosen model: e.g. nonlocal perception kernels, delay terms, and any regularity assumptions are model-dependent and are not fixed by Open Problem 38 itself.
No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency data are relevant here; this is a PDE well-posedness question, not an algebraic one.
refined_question: For any previously introduced PDE model in this paper whose existence theory remains open, determine—within the natural solution class for that model and under its prescribed domain, boundary conditions, kernel/delay structure, and, for evolutionary problems, fixed initial data—whether there are necessary and/or sufficient conditions ensuring that the model admits a unique non-trivial solution once existence has been established.
justification: The draft matches Open Problem 38 almost verbatim, and it is closer to that broad official formulation than to the paper’s narrower model-specific uniqueness questions. The nearby context in §4.1.1-§4.1.2 defines what the paper means by existence and uniqueness, including the point that time-dependent uniqueness is relative to a fixed initial condition and that the relevant solution notion may be classical, weak, strong, or mild. Section 5.1 then supplies the practical scope of the phrase "previously introduced model with existence as an open problem" by summarizing which earlier models still lack well-posedness results and by noting contexts in which uniqueness has already been proved. Although §2.3.1 contains specific uniqueness open problems for models (2.21), (2.23), and (2.24), your draft is broader and therefore aligns best with Open Problem 38 rather than with any one of those narrower questions.
